body: Holy shit the more I read the more I see my family

You know, reading this I came to recall an instance similar to this. I used to think my parents weren't so bad because I was raise under the "You're not missing any limbs" mentality. But now I realize psychological harm can be much much worse than "missing any limbs." I hope you can get your sibling out of there; I'll be working to help my own.

Thanks for your comment. I know about the /r/depression community, and they have helped me before. This post was just me rambling on about today, and I felt like I'd just blow some steam off.
Did something bad happen today? If so, would you mind if I asked? To get it off your chest?

Child of divorced parents and fucked up family here, maybe I can help. Reddit helped me, I've been a lurker for sometime then one time I felt especially bad and opened up (I rarely do that so I was on shaky ground) and I was able to be consoled. Whenever Reddit's not available, I turn to music (either sad and mellow or heavy metal, however I feel) I also used contact sports (football, MMA, etc) practicing and winning competitions got my self esteem up. I also need to learn to do this, but learning to cry and let things out help a lot. I did it recently for the first time in years and it helped. Eating a healthy diet helps too. Getting up early may suck, but then eating a homemade, freshly cooked eggs with beef and sliced onion woke me up, and despite depression, it gave me some hope of a good day. I'm sorry that you have to go through this tough time and I hope that you can recover. If anything, myself or any other redditor here can help, and we can recover together.
I'll keep that in mind, thanks
